subject: Pricing & caching assumptions — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam@retailai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + caching/pricing questions

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sam — good conversation. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can put a pricing proposal together that matches your target economics.

Key notes from the call:
- You’re evaluating replacing your current inference path for product recommendations and short-form personalization.
- Expected production footprint (ballpark): monthly active traffic concentrated in US, with spikes at campaign times.
- Your procurement timeline: decision in 4–6 weeks, pilot first, then production in Q1.

To get a tighter proposal we need two quick datapoints from your side (see inline):
1) Monthly token volumes (prompt + completion) — baseline and peak. If you can provide a 2–3 week sample or even a ballpark monthly estimate that’s ideal.
2) Target unit economics: what effective $/1M tokens are you trying to hit (after any caching or batching effects)? You mentioned a mid-single-digit target on the call but I want to confirm a range (e.g., $5–$12 / 1M tokens).
3) Caching behavior: what % of requests are templated/prefixable vs fully freeform? Any telemetry on repeated prefixes or stable system prompts will help us estimate prefix cache hit rate.

To be transparent about how caching moves the needle: our initial model assumes a prefix cache hit rate in the 25–40% range for LLM-driven product templates (higher for rigid templates). That hit rate directly reduces the paid token volume used for inference. We’ll run those numbers into the pricing hanger once you confirm volumes and target unit cost.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short pricing deck and SOC2 summary for procurement — will send an updated quote once we have the numbers above.

Next steps:
- You: send token volume estimate and target $/1M range.
- Us: we’ll return an effective-cost model (showing list $/1M, cache hit-rate scenarios, and resulting effective $/1M) and a 30-day pilot proposal.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Redwood Inference

From: Sam Taylor <sam@retailai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@retailai.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + caching/pricing questions

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Below are the numbers we can share right now (rough but accurate enough for a proposal):

1) Volume (prod inference)
- Baseline month: ~150M total tokens (prompt + completion).
- Peak month (campaigns): up to ~420M tokens.
- Typical session: 12–18 tokens prompt + 28–60 tokens completion depending on user flow.

2) Target unit economics
- We’re aiming for an effective cost in the $8–$12 per 1M tokens range (post any caching/batching). If you can get us below $8 that would be ideal but we’re prepared to evaluate in the quoted range.

3) Caching/prefix behavior
- About 35–45% of requests are highly templated (same prefix + variable user slot) — these should be prefix-cacheable.
- Another ~15% are repeated completions (same user journey) where a session/KV cache could help. The remaining requests are freeform.

We don’t have exact hit-rate telemetry yet; our infra team can extract sample logs if necessary. For procurement: we want a sample price model showing list price, assumed cache hit rates (25%, 35%, 50%), and resulting effective $/1M. Also include pilot terms (30-day, capped tokens) and any volume discounts.

Happy to hop on a 30–45m follow-up if that helps speed things up.

Best,
Sam Taylor
Head of Product
RetailAI
sam@retailai.com
(617) 555-9876

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam@retailai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@retailai.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + caching/pricing questions

Thanks Sam — this is perfect. I’ve modeled three scenarios below so procurement has a clear apples-to-apples comparison. I’ll attach a one-page that shows the math and we’ll include it in the formal quote.

Assumptions (example list price for compute): $15.00 per 1M tokens (list)
Scenarios (effective cost after prefix cache hit):
- 25% hit: effective = $15 * (1 - 0.25) = $11.25 per 1M
- 35% hit: effective = $15 * (1 - 0.35) = $9.75 per 1M
- 50% hit: effective = $15 * (1 - 0.50) = $7.50 per 1M

Notes on the model and why it’s conservative:
- The model above treats cache hit as a direct reduction in charged tokens since a cached prefix avoids repeated attention computation for the cached token span.
- Additional levers that lower effective price: batching improvements (esp. for campaigns), quantized model variants for cheaper tiers, and KV caching for session continuity. We’ll show a combined sensitivity table in the quote.
- For RetailAI’s stated mix (35–45% templated + ~15% session repeats), a combined 35%+ overall hit is a reasonable baseline; that maps to ~ $9.75/1M on the $15 list example — inside your $8–$12 target. If we can drive toward the 45–50% range with prefix tuning and pilot instrumentation, we can hit the low-$7s.

Pilot proposal (30 days)
- Tokens: capped at 200M tokens for the pilot month (covers baseline + some burst).
- Instrumentation: we’ll add cache-hit metrics at the route level, show token and CPU savings, and export sample traces for your infra team.
- Pricing: trial list price with holdback discounts applied based on measured hit-rate (we’ll reconcile post-pilot).
- Deliverables: post-pilot report with measured hit rates, effective $/1M, recommendations for prompt templating to improve hit rates.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send a formal quote and one-pager with the three-hit-rate scenarios + pilot terms (attached).
2) If Procurement agrees, we can issue a short SOW / pilot order and schedule kickoff next week.
3) Marcus will own the pilot onboarding — Marcus, I’ll loop you for scheduling.

If that all sounds good I’ll prepare the DocuSign and pricing sheet for Procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
